newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Fischler to force vets vote on ban of suspect sheep tissue.
newsitem.headline: Fischler to force vets vote on ban of suspect sheep tissue.

text.p: The European Union's Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler intends on Friday to force a vote on a controversial proposal to remove suspect tissue from sheep and goats, Commission officials said.
The EU's Standing Veterinary Committee, composed of chief veterinary officers from the 15 member states, will be asked to reconsider a proposal it rejected on August 1.
"The proposal is being blocked by some member states, including Germany, and the Commissioner intends to force a vote," an official said.
Germany, supported by six other member states, argued that there is no BSE in German cattle and that the measure was economically unacceptable as there was only a slight public health risk.
Only Britain, France and Ireland previously expressed any support for the proposal, based on advice from the Scientific Veterinary Committee.
The proposal followed British and French research showing that sheep could catch mad cow disease, or Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), raising public health fears.
Sheep have for centuries been know to suffer from scrapie, a brain wasting disease similar to BSE, which can be passed from one animal to another and from ewe to lamb but not to humans.
If on Friday there is no qualified majority in support of the proposal, it will be sent to the Farm Council on December 9-10 when it could be adopted by a simple majority.
The vice chairman of the Parliament's consumer protection committee, Conservative MEP Caroline Jackson, told Reuters in a telephone interview on Thursday:
"This is a very urgent issue of human health and it is shameful that Germany should be putting the interests of its own beef industry first.
"So long as there is the slightest suspicion then it is essential that all suspect tissue be removed." REUTER
